title.value: Maximal Initial Learning Rates in Deep ReLU Networks
title.justification: The title reflects the core focus of the paper, which is about understanding the largest initial learning rates for deep ReLU networks.
title.quote: Maximal Initial Learning Rates in Deep ReLU Networks

extractions.description: The paper explores the concept of the maximal initial learning rate in deep learning, specifically in fully-connected ReLU networks. It introduces the maximal initial learning rate η∗, which is the largest rate at which a network can begin training successfully. The authors analyze how this rate is determined by the architecture of the network, specifically the depth and width, and its relationship to the sharpness λ1 of the network at initialization. They provide empirical and theoretical insights into how η∗ can be computed and how it behaves differently from learning rates in later stages of training.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper is concerned primarily with improving deep learning model training efficiency, with no direct mention of climate or ecological sustainability applications.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Training a neural network requires choosing a suitable learning rate, which involves a trade-off between speed and effectiveness of convergence.

secondary_categories.quote: Our main contributions are as follows: In §3.1, we introduce the maximal initial learning rate η ∗ – the largest learning rate at which a randomly initialized neural network can successfully begin training – and show how it can be computed.
